title: How To Plan A Multi-shaft Loom Weaving Project
How To Read A Weaving Draft
summary: Learn how to read a weaving draft for a multi-shaft loom.
content:
A weaving draft for a multi-shaft loom instructs the weaver how to set-up and operate a multi-shaft loom to weave a cloth. A weaving draft is a kin to a cable chart within a knitting pattern, though it doesn't give all of the instructions for the knitting pattern such as gauge and weight of yarn the cable chart does instruct the knitter how to knit the more complex parts of the knitting pattern. A weaving draft doesn't usually include EPI or the weight of thread/yarn intended for the cloth, however the weaving draft does instruct the weaver how to heddle the warp, how to tie up the treadle peddles, and what treadle peddle is needed for each pick in order to weave the desired cloth.
The anatomy of a weaving draft is relatively simple with four quadrants known as the threading, tie-up, treadling, and draw-down.
### Threading The threading is located in the top left of a weaving draft. The vertical columns represent each individual thread of the warp, and the horizontal rows represent the shafts of the multi-shaft loom. **The threading is read right to left, and bottom up with the first shaft being the bottom most row and the very first end/thread as the rightmost column.** Directly above the threading you can find the warp colors. The threading can only ever have one shaft selected as a warp thread should only be heddled in one shaft and one shaft only. ### Tie-up The tie-up is located in the top right of a weaving draft. The tie-up instructs the weaver which shaft needs to be tied up to each treadle peddle to lift (or sink) the shafts needed to weave a pick with a single simple press of a peddle. **The tie up is read left to right, the individual treadle peddles are the vertical columns and the shafts of the loom are the horizontal rows just as it's represented in the threading to the left of the tie-up. The bottom-most row is the first shaft of the loom, and the left most column is the first treadle peddle.** ### **Treadling** The treadling is located in the bottom right of a weaving draft. The treadling instructs the weaver which treadle peddle to compress with each pick, and also what weft color to use for a weft pick, with the weft colors being to the right of the treadling. **The treadling is read left to right and top down.** Just as with the tie-up the treadle peddles are read left to right with the left most column being the first treadle peddle. The very first pick is the first row. ### Draw-Down The draw-down is located in the bottom left of a weaving draft. The draw-down gives an example of what the woven cloth will look like. With modern weaving draft applications the draw-down display begins to come together once the threading, tie-up, and treadling are filled in. > [!IMPORTANT] > Most weaving draft making applications show a draw-down for a rising shaft loom only and do not have an option to make a weaving draft for a sinking shaft loom. Therefore if you're using a weaving draft application that does not allow for a sinking shaft tie-up but want to know what the cloth will look like you'll want to invert your tie up. That is to say if you need to sink shafts two and four with a four shaft loom with sinking shafts then in the tie up of a weaving draft application that does not give an option for a sinking shaft loom you'll want to select shafts one and three instead. Most weaving draft applications do not have a tie up option for a counter-march loom either which both sinks and lifts shafts and requires for every single shaft to be tied up to the treadle peddles. In that case, the weaver would want to use the filled in boxes of the tie up to be their lower lamms that raise the shaft and the shafts not filled in would be the upper lamms of the shaft.
